title: ELISA (Enzyme-Linked Immunosorbent Assay) — Principle & Workflow

references.label: WHO Laboratory Quality Management System Handbook

purpose: To detect and often quantify a specific antigen or antibody in a sample using an antibody-antigen binding step coupled to an enzyme-generated, measurable color (or other) signal.
principle: A capture molecule (antibody or antigen, depending on assay design) is bound to a solid-phase well; the sample is added and, if the target is present, it binds; an enzyme-linked detection reagent then binds to the captured target; and a substrate is added that the enzyme converts into a colored (or fluorescent/chemiluminescent) product, read photometrically — the same absorbance-based measurement principle the laboratory already covers generically, applied to an immunological detection reaction rather than a chemical one. Signal intensity relates to the amount of target present, commonly interpreted against a cutoff (qualitative) or a standard curve (quantitative), depending on assay design.

procedure.instruction: Add sample, and required controls, to the antigen- or antibody-coated wells and incubate per the assay's specified time/temperature.
Wash unbound material from the wells thoroughly — inadequate washing is one of the most common sources of false-positive signal.
Add the enzyme-conjugated detection reagent and incubate.
Wash again, then add substrate/chromogen and incubate for color development in the dark (many chromogens are light-sensitive) for the assay's specified time.
Add stop solution at the specified time to halt the enzymatic reaction consistently across all wells.

procedure.note: Controls must fall within their expected range before any patient result on that plate is interpreted — an out-of-range control invalidates the run.
procedure.instruction: Read absorbance on a plate reader at the assay's specified wavelength and interpret against the manufacturer's cutoff or standard curve, including verifying that control wells performed as expected before interpreting patient results.

observations: Record absorbance values for all wells including controls; note plate uniformity (edge effects, streaking) that could indicate a technical problem.
interpretation: Result is interpreted relative to the assay's validated cutoff or standard curve, only after confirming controls performed within their expected range; a single ELISA result is often a screening result requiring a confirmatory method for definitive interpretation, per the assay's intended use.
precautions: Thorough, consistent washing at every wash step is essential to result validity.
Protect light-sensitive substrates from light during color development.
limitations: Cross-reactivity with structurally similar antigens can cause false positives; very early infection (before adequate antibody/antigen levels) can cause false negatives — these limitations are assay-specific and documented in the manufacturer's package insert.
biosafetyNotes: Handle all patient samples as potentially infectious; follow standard precautions and dispose of used plates/reagents per biohazard and chemical waste protocols.
